Second pilot report: the three aims, and the fix for false rewiring

A review document: the pilot, its results, the spec, and the decisions log

Published

November 13, 2026

Summary

Scope. This document reports the second pilot1 of the project, for revision 1 of the proposal (proposal.md, section 12), which restored the user’s three aims: pregnancy stage, disease activity at each visit, and whether edges change differently in SLE than in RA across pregnancy. It covers the idea, how the pilot was run, what it found, the project spec, and the decisions made along the way. It was built from project-spec.md, decisions.md, the saved results in pilot-b/results/, the factor shift measured on GSE235508 (results/factor_shift.rds), and, read-only, the first pilot’s results in pilot/results/; every number is computed from those files when the document renders.

Status. In STATUS.md the second pilot is marked piloted-close-call2. Every clause the rule names as deciding passed: the fix, the equivalence of edges and their formula, and the removal of the activity artifact. Two clauses about size at the study’s levels failed and two were close calls.

Pilot question Answer Key evidence
1. Does the fix work? pass, pass, pass Raw edges called 0.170 (MCSE 0.0045) of factor pairs changed at the stress level; partial edges gave 0.0476 to 0.0485 across the five factor-only cells (nominal 0.05), and kept 0.223 (MCSE 0.0107) of a real module change against 0.231 (MCSE 0.0111) for raw edges.
2. Does it matter at the study’s levels? close call, fail, close call False rewiring: 0.049 (MCSE 0.0011) at the SLE level, 0.107 (MCSE 0.0033) at the RA level; false SLE-against-RA difference 0.079 (MCSE 0.0022); a real SLE-only change found in 0.157 (MCSE 0.0076) of module pairs by partial edges.
3. Prediction pass, pass, fail N1 against F1 ranged over -0.0007 to 0.0004 in cells 1 to 7; for activity, N1 against E1 was 0.0020 (MCSE 0.0016) when only the IFN factor’s spread tracked activity, and 0.0034 (MCSE 0.0020) when the module’s correlation did.

What needs your decision (details in Action items and limitations): the status call; whether the pregnancy work enters the one paper as its second application; the analysis of activity within woman at stage 3; and the open [TO CONFIRM] items in the spec (highlighted in yellow).

The idea

In plain language

LIONESS3 gives every blood sample a value for every pair of genes, called an edge. When the edges of the same women differ between pregnancy and the months after birth, the difference is read as the immune network “rewiring”. But an edge is, almost exactly, a simple product of the sample’s own two gene values, so anything that moves many genes together, such as the interferon4 response or the mix of white cells, changes the edges by its square. Suppose two genes that follow the white-cell mix are each 1 unit above average after birth and 1.5 units above in pregnancy: their product rises from 1 to 2.25, and the edge “rewires” with no change in how the genes work together.

The fix tested here removes the interferon score and the cell mix from each gene before the edge is built (a partial correlation5). The pilot simulates women followed through pregnancy, with interferon and cell-mix changes as large as those measured in the real study, and asks three things: whether the usual before-and-after test of edges calls false rewiring and whether the fix stops it; whether edges predict pregnancy stage or disease activity beyond simpler models; and whether a false difference between lupus and arthritis appears and disappears with the fix. No edge was computed on patient data.

Potential impact

LIONESS builds one network per sample and has an R implementation (M. L. Kuijjer et al. 2019; Marieke L. Kuijjer et al. 2019); its authors propose sample networks for studying change across time. The first-order term of the edge is the influence function of the correlation (Devlin et al. 1975), the product term is the iENA edge (Yu et al. 2017), and a recent review relates sample edges to covariance products (Kuijjer et al. 2026). The study behind the data described pregnancy in SLE and RA by differential expression and deconvolution (Lien et al. 2024); no single-sample network analysis of pregnancy was found at stage 1.

The problem is the reading of a change in edges between time points, or between diseases, as rewiring, when the factors that move many genes at once change too. The pilot shows the size of it and a fix. At a large factor change, raw edges called 0.170 (MCSE 0.0045) of the pairs whose co-expression never changed “rewired”; the partial-correlation edges called 0.048 (MCSE 0.0010), the test’s own level, and in every factor-only cell the fixed share stayed within 0.0476 to 0.0485 (Table 4). The fix kept a real change: 0.223 (MCSE 0.0107) of the module pairs against 0.231 (MCSE 0.0111) for raw edges, and 0.157 (MCSE 0.0076) for a real SLE-only change between diseases.

At the factor changes measured in GSE235508 the artifact is modest: none at the SLE level, 0.107 (MCSE 0.0033) at the RA level, and 0.079 (MCSE 0.0022) for a false SLE-against-RA difference, all brought back to the nominal level by the fix (Figure 4). In prediction, edges equalled their first-order formula for pregnancy stage and for activity (N1 against F1 within -0.0007 to 0.0004), and the base with the squared score removed the artifact from activity prediction. A user who reports rewiring over pregnancy, or a disease difference in rewiring, would apply the partial-correlation edges first; the impact for the paper is a fix that works at the stress level and at the real levels alike, with a real-data illustration whose effect is about twice the nominal rate in RA.

Application: the study behind the data

The study

The data come from a Norwegian longitudinal study of pregnancy in rheumatic disease (Lien et al. 2024), https://doi.org/10.1136/ard-2023-224644, GEO series GSE2355086. Women with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)7, rheumatoid arthritis (RA)8, and healthy women gave whole-blood samples for RNA sequencing before pregnancy, in each trimester, and at 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months after birth, with disease activity recorded at each visit (DAS289 in RA, LAI-P10 in SLE). The paper reports that the interferon signature was augmented in SLE pregnancy and that the altered cell type composition strongly influences the profile. Table 1 counts the women with samples in both periods, and Table 2 gives the size of the factor change measured in this project from the counts.

Why the share of pairs called changed

The quantity that decides the first and third aims is the share of gene pairs that a test calls changed: across pregnancy within the same women (aim 1), or differently in SLE than in RA (aim 3). With no change in co-expression the share should be 5%, the test’s level; a higher share is false rewiring. The second aim is judged by the concordance index11 of predicted against observed activity, the continuous counterpart of the AUC12.

Did the original study compute it?

No. The original study used differential expression and cell-type deconvolution, and reported no expression pattern attributable to disease activity; it computed no co-expression or single-sample network and made no test of rewiring.

In symbols

The standardized expression of gene \(i\) in sample \(q\) (\(z_{qi}\)), the reference correlation (\(r\)), the shared factors (\(F_q\), \(C_q\), with loadings \(\lambda\)), and the conditioning set (\(S_q\), the IFN score and composition) determine the LIONESS edge (\(e_q\)), its first-order form, its mean given the factor, and the partial-correlation edge (\(e^{\text{p}}_q\)):

\[ \begin{aligned} e_q &= N r - (N-1)\, r_{(-q)} = r + z_{qi} z_{qj} - \frac{r}{2}\left(z_{qi}^2 + z_{qj}^2\right) + O_p\left(N^{-1}\right), \\ \mathrm{E}\left[e_q \mid F_q\right] &= \text{const} + \left[\lambda_i \lambda_j - \frac{r}{2}\left(\lambda_i^2 + \lambda_j^2\right)\right] F_q^2 + O\left(N^{-1}\right), \\ e^{\text{p}}_q &= N \rho - (N-1)\, \rho_{(-q)}, \quad \rho = \mathrm{cor}\left(x_i - \hat x_i(S), \, x_j - \hat x_j(S)\right). \end{aligned} \]

Symbol Meaning
\(z_{qi}\) expression of gene \(i\) in sample \(q\), standardized by the reference
\(r\), \(r_{(-q)}\) correlation of genes \(i\) and \(j\) in the reference, and without sample \(q\)
\(F_q\), \(\lambda_i\) shared factor in sample \(q\) and gene \(i\)’s loading on it
\(S_q\) the conditioning set: the IFN score and composition
\(\rho\), \(e^{\text{p}}_q\) partial correlation given \(S\), and its LIONESS edge

The target is the change in correlation between periods; the raw edge’s change adds the bracket times the change in \(\mathrm{E}[F^2]\). The partial edge removes \(F\) from each gene first, so its change carries no \(F^2\) term, up to the error with which the score measures \(F\).

Critiquing the model

Any model is a simplification, and the useful question is not whether it is true but where it bends and whether the bend matters for the question being asked. The model above was chosen so that the problem could be written as a formula and checked by simulation, and each simplification that made that possible is a place where real data may behave differently. The table lists the main ones. Work through it one row at a time. The first column names the feature and the symbols in the equations that carry it, so find them there first. Then decide in your own words how the feature could fail for real data before reading the second column, and finally read the third column for what should be done to check it. Several of these checks are natural first tasks for the project. Which of them the pilot examined, and which it left open, is for you to find when you read the Methods and Results that follow.

Feature of the model Why it may not be realistic What should be done to check it
Two shared factors with equal loadings (0.8 IFN, 0.6 composition) Blood has several cell types and IFN subtypes, with different loadings per gene Estimate the factors and loadings from GSE235508 and plant changes in real data (a plasmode)
Factor levels from one score each (IFN5, a principal component) The principal component is a rough proxy for composition Use marker-gene scores for neutrophils, lymphocytes, and monocytes
Composition observed without error Composition is estimated, so the partial edge removes it only partly Add measurement error to \(C\)
Four samples per woman, two in each period The study has up to seven uneven time points Mirror each woman’s real time points
Activity with a woman-level part, predicted across women Activity differs between women more than within, so across-woman prediction is weak Analyse activity within woman
Normal noise Log counts have heavier tails Resample residuals from the real data

Methods

Design

The pilot simulates women followed through pregnancy in 10 cells, three aims. Each woman gives four samples. Fifty genes: genes 1 to 20 follow the IFN factor \(F\) (the IFN score is the mean of genes 1 to 5), genes 21 to 30 form a co-expressed module, and genes 31 to 50 follow the composition factor \(C\). Both factors may shift and spread in pregnancy, by the amounts measured in SLE or in RA (Table 2), or by a large stress amount. In aim 1 and aim 3 cells, LIONESS edges (raw) and partial-correlation edges (the fix) are computed on each disease’s samples, and each woman’s change in edge between periods is tested. In aim 1 and aim 2 cells, six models predict pregnancy stage or activity with 5-fold cross-validation13 by woman.

Each figure and table in the Results traces back to one row of this diagram.

Part Cells Main factors Replicates
A 1 to 5 levels none, SLE, RA, stress; module +0.4 200 per cell
B 6 and 7 activity linked to the IFN factor’s spread or to the module 200 per cell
C 8 to 10 SLE against RA; module +0.4 in SLE; stress 200 per cell

The six models are \(R_0\) (composition and the residual IFN score), \(R_1\) (\(R_0\) with both squares), and elastic nets14 with the \(R_1\) terms unpenalized: E1 (the 45 non-score genes), F1 (E1 with the 990 first-order edges), N1 (E1 with the 990 LIONESS edges), and N1 with \(R_0\) (the edges on \(R_0\), to show the artifact). Pregnancy stage is scored by the AUC, activity by the concordance index, with the correlation, out-of-fold \(R^2\), and root mean squared error reported.

Known-answer checks

Known-answer checks come before any result, because every later number is only as good as the simulation that produced it. Each check sets up a case where the correct answer is known from theory, runs the simulation code on it, and compares the two. Agreement says nothing about the scientific question or about real data. It says that the code does what the model says. Disagreement means stopping to look for a bug before reading anything else, and the same checks apply to any code you write for the project.

Read each row of the table in four steps: the setting that was simulated, the known answer for that setting, what the simulation gave, and whether the gap between the two is small compared with the Monte Carlo standard error (MCSE). The MCSE is how much a simulated result moves from run to run because only a finite number of replicates was used. A gap within about two MCSE is noise, and a gap of several MCSE is a problem.

0 of 10 rows with a standard error are more than 2 MCSE from the known value.

Results

How to read the outputs

Each output traces back to a row of the design diagram (the captions name the part where one applies). Read each in the same four steps. First, find its row in the diagram, which says what was simulated and what was varied. Second, work out what one point or one table entry is, usually one combination of the varied factors, averaged over replicates. Third, identify the reference value that would hold if nothing were wrong, shown as a dashed or grey line wherever possible. Fourth, look for where the results leave that reference, and for which settings they do. The outputs report three kinds of quantity.

  • Bias is the average of an estimate minus its true value. When the truth is no difference, any average difference from 0 is a spurious difference created by the problem under study.
  • Level is how often a test rejects when there is truly nothing to find. A correct test at 0.05 rejects 5% of the time, so a rate above 0.05 means too many false alarms.
  • Power is how often a test rejects when there is a real effect. More is better, but only when the level is not inflated, because a test that rejects too often also looks powerful.

All rates and averages come from simulation, so each carries Monte Carlo error. That is why the figures show bars or a grey band, and why small differences should not be over-read.

This pilot reports shares of gene pairs called changed (a rate whose correct value with no change in co-expression is 0.05), the AUC, the concordance index, and paired differences between models. A paired difference is computed within each replicate and then averaged; its MCSE is the replicate standard deviation of the difference divided by the square root of the number of replicates.

False rewiring and the fix

Figure guide (parts A and C). Each row is one cell; the left panel shows factor pairs (genes whose co-expression never changes), the right panel module pairs (genes whose co-expression changes in cells 5 and 9). Red circles are raw LIONESS edges, blue triangles partial-correlation edges; the dashed line is the 5% a correct test should give with no change. Look for: whether the red circles sit right of the line in the factor panel; whether the blue triangles sit on it; whether the blue triangles stay close to the red circles in the module panel where the change is real.

Prediction

Figure guide (parts A and B). Each row is one prediction cell; the points are paired differences in AUC (cells 1 to 5) or concordance (cells 6 and 7) averaged over 200 replicates, with bars of two MCSE: N1 with \(R_0\) against \(R_0\) (the artifact), N1 against E1, N1 against F1. Look for: whether the purple points sit on the line in every row; where the red points sit away from it; whether the blue points move away from the line in cell 7.

Numbered findings

Each finding is a claim followed by the output behind it. Read the claim, open the output, and check that you can see the claim there before accepting it.

  1. Raw edges call false rewiring, in proportion to the factor change. With no change in co-expression, the share of factor pairs called changed was 0.049 (MCSE 0.0011) at the SLE level, 0.107 (MCSE 0.0033) at the RA level, and 0.170 (MCSE 0.0045) at the stress level (Table 4, red circles in Figure 4).
  2. The fix brings the false rewiring back to the test’s level. Partial-correlation edges gave 0.0476 to 0.0485 in every factor-only cell, within a disease and between diseases (Table 6, clause 1(b)).
  3. The fix keeps a real change. With the module’s correlation rising in pregnancy, partial edges called 0.223 (MCSE 0.0107) of module pairs changed, raw edges 0.231 (MCSE 0.0111) (clause 1(c)).
  4. A false SLE-against-RA difference appears at the real levels and the fix removes it. Raw edges called 0.079 (MCSE 0.0022) of factor pairs differently changed, partial edges 0.048 (MCSE 0.0009); a real SLE-only change was found in 0.157 (MCSE 0.0076) of module pairs by partial edges, within 3 MCSE of the 0.15 threshold (clauses 2(b), 2(c)).
  5. Edges equal their formula in prediction. N1 and F1 differed by -0.0007 to 0.0004 in AUC or concordance across cells 1 to 7 (clause 3(a), purple points in Figure 5).
  6. The base with the squared score removes the activity artifact, but edges do not find activity-linked co-expression across women. When activity raised only the IFN factor’s spread, N1 with \(R_0\) gained 0.043 (MCSE 0.0031) over \(R_0\) in concordance and N1 added 0.0020 (MCSE 0.0016) over E1; when activity raised the module’s correlation, N1 added 0.0034 (MCSE 0.0020), below 0.03, and every model’s concordance was below 0.5 there (Table 5; decisions log, D3).
  7. The known-answer checks hold. Every identity agreed to better than \(10^{-13}\), and in the null cell the shares sat at the test’s level and the AUCs near 0.5 (Table 3).

Tables

Table guide (shares). One row per testing cell: the mean share of pairs called changed, with its MCSE, for raw and partial edges, factor and module pairs. The reference value is 0.05 wherever co-expression does not change.

Table guide (prediction). One row per prediction cell; the columns are the mean out-of-fold AUC (cells 1 to 5) or concordance index (cells 6 and 7) of each model. The reference value is 0.5 for no prediction.

The largest MCSE of an entry in the table is 0.0054. In the activity cells, the out-of-fold \(R^2\) of N1 was -0.090 and -0.101, and its root mean squared error 1.016 and 1.037 (activity has unit variance).

Table guide (the verdict). One row per clause of the pre-registered rule, read by pilot-b/verdict.R. Check that each outcome follows from its value and threshold, and that the combination gives the status.

1. Question and why it matters

Question (one sentence): Do LIONESS edges separate pregnant from non-pregnant samples of the same women beyond the IFN score, cell composition, their squares, the gene levels, and their own first-order features, and does the answer differ between SLE and RA?

Why it matters: A change in LIONESS edges over pregnancy is read as rewiring of immune co-expression. If the mechanism holds, much of that change is the squared change of the factors pregnancy moves (composition in every woman, IFN in SLE), and a user would fit the base with the squared score and the gene levels before claiming that edges add anything, and would check every network result against the first-order formula.

2. Mechanism we suspect

A LIONESS edge equals, to first order, \(r + z_{qi} z_{qj} - \tfrac{r}{2}(z_{qi}^2 + z_{qj}^2)\). Under a shared factor \(F\) with loadings \(\lambda\), its conditional mean is linear in \(F_q^2\) with coefficient \(\lambda_i \lambda_j - \tfrac{r}{2}(\lambda_i^2 + \lambda_j^2)\), so the difference in mean edge between pregnancy and the postpartum period is that coefficient times the difference in \(\mathrm{E}[F^2]\), with the period-specific correlation unchanged. The gap is zero when pregnancy moves neither the mean nor the spread of \(F\) (the null cell), and grows with the shift and the scale of \(F\) (the factor cells). If the mechanism is wrong, edges would gain over E1 in factor-only cells, or edges and the first-order formula would classify differently.

3. Pilot

Code: pilot/pilot.R (Rscript pilot/pilot.R --reps <n>), then Rscript pilot/verdict.R; data description Rscript pilot/describe_data.R.

Pass rule: pilot/preregistration.md, section 2, copied from proposal section 7.

Verdict file: pilot/results/verdict.rds, after the run.

Plot: pilot/results/auc_gains.png; pilot-b: pilot-b/results/shares.png, pilot-b/results/model_gains.png.

Second pilot (pilot-b/, proposal section 12, the user’s three aims): piloted-close-call (2026-11-13), 200 replicates per cell, 10 cells, three cores, 965 seconds; verdict file pilot-b/results/verdict.rds. Numbers rounded from pilot-b/results/cell_summaries.rds.

  1. Does the fix work? Yes: raw edges called 0.17 of unchanged factor pairs changed at the stress level; partial-correlation edges gave 0.044 to 0.049 in every factor-only cell, within and between diseases, and kept a real module change (0.22 against 0.23).
  2. Does it matter at the study’s levels? Modestly: no false rewiring at the SLE level, 0.107 at the RA level (close call), a false SLE-against-RA difference of 0.079 (below 0.10, fail), and a real SLE-only change found in 0.157 of module pairs (close call).
  3. Prediction: edges equalled their formula (N1 against F1 within 0.0007); the base with the squared score removed the activity artifact; edges did not detect activity-linked co-expression across women (fail).

Status: piloted-close-call (2026-11-13), 200 replicates per cell, 8 cells, three cores, 1,622 seconds.

The three pilot answers (pilot/results/verdict.rds; numbers rounded from pilot/results/cell_summaries.rds):

  1. Does the effect exist? Edges equal their formula: N1 and F1 differed by at most 0.0011 in AUC in any cell (1(b) pass). With a module change at 40 women, N1 gained 0.043 (MCSE 0.0039) over E1, within 3 MCSE of 0.05 (1(a) close call).
  2. Is it large enough at realistic sizes? Not by classification at 20 women: the artifact was 0.005 (MCSE 0.0035), below 0.02 (2(a) fail), and real rewiring added 0.009 (MCSE 0.0034) over E1, below 0.03 (2(b) fail). By the paired edge test, yes: with no change in co-expression, 0.45 of factor-gene pairs were called rewired at 20 women under a large factor change, against 0.047 in the null cell.
  3. Is there a fix? For classification, yes: with the E1 base edges added between -0.0004 and 0.0015 in the factor-only cells (3(a) pass). For the paired edge test, none was tested.

4. ADEMP skeleton

Aims. (1) Do LIONESS edges and their first-order formula classify pregnancy stage alike? (2) How much do edges gain from a factor that changes over pregnancy, and does the E1 base remove it? (3) When co-expression truly changes, do edges detect it beyond E1 at the study’s size?

Data-generating mechanisms.

  • Factors varied, with levels: what pregnancy changes (nothing; the factor \(F\), moderate or large; the module’s correlation by 0.2 or 0.4; both); the number of women (20, 40).
  • Factors fixed, and why: four samples per woman (two in each period, the median the study provides per disease); 50 genes (as in the first project, so results are comparable); loadings 0.8 and 0.4; woman-level gene offsets of variance 0.5 (the between-person part of whole-blood expression); normal noise (heavy tails were tested in the first project).
  • A cell where the answer is known: the null cell, every AUC 0.5.

Estimands. The out-of-sample AUC of each model for the period of a new woman’s sample; the paired AUC differences \(\Delta_1\), \(\Delta_2\), and the artifact \(G\).

Methods compared. \(R_0\), \(R_1\) (logistic); E1, E5, F1, N1, N1 with \(R_0\) (elastic net, glmnet cv.glmnet, mixing 0.5, 5 inner folds grouped by woman, binomial deviance, lambda.min, base terms unpenalized). Outer 5-fold cross-validation by woman.

Performance measures. Mean out-of-fold AUC and paired differences with MCSE; the share of gene pairs called different between periods by a paired test (apparent rewiring).

Replicates and Monte Carlo SE target. 200 per cell in the pilot if the time box allows, an MCSE of about 0.003 for a difference with standard deviation 0.04.

5. Application

Dataset: GSE235508 (Lien et al. 2024), GEO; the series matrix in data/raw/ for the pilot’s description, the counts at stage 3 after approval.

Comparison: within SLE and within RA separately, pregnant (trimesters 1 to 3) against non-pregnant (pre-pregnancy and postpartum) samples of the same women, folds by woman; counts per group from pilot/results/data_summary.rds.

What to show: whether the apparent rewiring over pregnancy, and any gain of edges over the base, disappears once the squared IFN and composition scores and the gene levels are in the base, and whether that differs between SLE and RA.

Decisions log

This is the agent’s decisions.md for the second pilot, read from the file when the document renders.

D0. The literature pass

As for the first pilot (pilot/decisions.md, D0). Read since: the GSE235508 counts and sample records for the factor shift (results/factor_shift.rds), and one search for other pregnancy datasets with SLE and RA (logged in log/02-pilot.md); none was found.

D1. The status call: piloted-close-call, with both readings

Every clause the rule names as deciding passed: the fix (1(b)), the equivalence of edges and their formula (3(a)), and the removal of the activity artifact by the E1 base (3(b)). Two clauses failed and two were close calls; values in pilot-b/results/verdict.rds.

  • The reading that passes. The paper’s claims held in every cell: partial-correlation edges brought the share of factor pairs called changed back to its nominal 5% in every cell where only the shared factors moved, within a disease and between diseases, at the real levels and at the stress level, while keeping nearly all of a real change (1(b), 1(c)). Edges equalled their first-order formula for pregnancy stage and for activity (3(a)). The failures are about size at the study’s levels: the false SLE-against-RA difference was above its nominal level but below the 0.10 threshold (2(b)), and the false rewiring at the RA level was within 3 MCSE of 0.10 (2(a), close). An artifact at about twice the nominal rate, removed by the fix, is a real-data illustration a methods paper can use.
  • The reading that fails. At the levels measured in GSE235508 the artifact is modest: none at the SLE level, where the IFN score barely moves and is stable within women (cell_summaries.rds, cell 2), about twice the nominal rate at the RA level (cell 3), and about one and a half times between diseases (cell 8). And aim 2 cannot be answered by prediction at 36 women: edges did not detect an activity-linked change in co-expression (3(c) fail), and every model’s concordance in that cell was below 0.5.

The agent’s reading: the close call is a pass for the paper’s methodological claims and a fail for clinical prediction of activity in this dataset. The user decides.

D2. Why the SLE level shows no false rewiring

At the SLE level the IFN factor’s shift (0.2) and spread ratio (1.1) change \(\mathrm{E}[F^2]\) by about 0.25 in units of the non-pregnant variance, and its within-woman correlation of 0.9 leaves little within-woman change for the paired test to see; the composition factor barely moves. The RA level moves composition by a shift of 0.45 and a spread ratio of 1.45, a change in \(\mathrm{E}[C^2]\) of about 1.3, which is where the false rewiring comes from. This is the theory’s prediction (the artifact scales with the change in the squared factor), visible across cells 2, 3, and 4.

D3. The activity cells: concordance below 0.5

In cell 7 every model’s pooled out-of-fold concordance was below 0.5, and the out-of-fold \(R^2\) was negative in cells 6 and 7 (cell_summaries.rds). Activity has a woman-level part (half its variance); with folds by woman, each held-out woman’s level is unknown to the model, and the training mean moves opposite to the held-out women’s mean, which biases pooled out-of-fold predictions downward against the outcome. The paired differences the clauses judge share this bias. For stage 3, activity should be analysed within woman (each visit’s activity relative to the woman’s own mean), which removes the between-woman part; this is a reading for the design stop, not a change to this verdict.

D4. The artifact in activity prediction

In cell 6 the edges with \(R_0\) gained over \(R_0\), and \(R_1\) (with the squared score) gained more; with the E1 base edges added nothing (3(b) pass). The artifact the first project found in classification appears in a continuous outcome, and the same base removes it.

D5. Seeds and restart

The machine restarted once during this session, before the pilot-b run started; the run itself completed in one pass (pilot-b/results/run_info.rds, pilot-b/run.log). The pre-registration and the amendment were committed and pushed before the run.

D6. What was not done

  • No edge was computed on GSE235508; only the factor shift was measured.
  • One loading per factor, normal noise, four samples per woman.
  • No within-woman activity analysis (D3), no plasmode, no healthy pregnancies; these are stage 3 options.

Action items and limitations

Action items

  1. Decide the status. The rule gives piloted-close-call; both readings are in the decisions log (D1). Every deciding clause passed; the failures concern the artifact’s size at the study’s levels (2(b)) and activity prediction across women (3(c)).
  2. Decide how the pregnancy work enters the one paper as its second application (the user’s decision of 2026-11-13: one paper), through a protocol amendment in the first project.
  3. At stage 3, analyse activity within woman (decisions log, D3), and consider the strengtheners proposed on 2026-11-13: the dose-response check across SLE, RA, and healthy pregnancies, a plasmode on GSE235508, and a within-woman label permutation as a real-data negative control.
  4. Resolve the yellow [TO CONFIRM] items in the spec, and verify the citations; 3 still lacks its full text.

Limitations

  • Everything here is simulation; no edge was computed on GSE235508, only the factor shift.
  • The composition level comes from a principal component, a rough proxy; composition is observed without error in the simulation.
  • Two factors with equal loadings, normal noise, four samples per woman.
  • Activity prediction across women is biased toward zero at this size (D3).

Footnotes

  1. A pilot is a quick, small first run of the proposal’s simulation, done before the project goes further, to check that the idea is worth the time. It asks three questions: does the effect exist, is it large enough at realistic sample sizes, and is there an obvious fix or diagnostic? The proposal (proposal.md) holds the pilot plan and its pass criteria.↩︎

  2. piloted-pass means all three pilot questions got a clear yes. piloted-fail means at least one clearly did not, so the project should not go on as proposed. piloted-close-call means at least one answer could be read either way, so the call is stated both ways: the reading that passes and the reading that fails.↩︎

  3. LIONESS (Linear Interpolation to Obtain Network Estimates for Single Samples) builds a network from all samples and again without one sample, and scales the difference to give that sample’s network.↩︎

  4. Interferons are signalling proteins of the immune system; many genes respond to them together, and their summed expression, the interferon score, is high in many patients with lupus.↩︎

  5. A partial correlation is the correlation of two genes after the part of each that follows other variables (here the interferon score and the cell mix) has been removed by regression.↩︎

  6. The Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) is the public archive of the US National Center for Biotechnology Information for gene expression data; a series (GSE) holds one study’s samples.↩︎

  7. Systemic lupus erythematosus is an autoimmune disease that can affect skin, joints, kidneys, and blood, and often flares in pregnancy.↩︎

  8. Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease of the joints; seropositive patients carry rheumatoid factor or anti-citrullinated protein antibodies, seronegative patients do not. It often improves in pregnancy.↩︎

  9. DAS28 (Disease Activity Score in 28 joints) combines tender and swollen joint counts, a blood inflammation marker, and the patient’s global assessment; above 5.1 is high activity, below 2.6 remission.↩︎

  10. LAI-P is a lupus activity index adapted for pregnancy, which discounts features that pregnancy itself causes; 0 means no activity.↩︎

  11. The concordance index is the share of pairs of visits with different activity in which the visit with higher activity gets the higher prediction; 0.5 is chance and 1 is perfect, and for a yes-or-no outcome it equals the AUC.↩︎

  12. The area under the ROC curve is the probability that a randomly chosen pregnant sample gets a higher score than a randomly chosen non-pregnant one; 0.5 is chance and 1 is perfect separation.↩︎

  13. In cross-validation the data are split into folds, each model is fitted without one fold and scored on it, and the scores are pooled; here every sample of a woman is in the same fold, so a woman’s own samples never help predict each other.↩︎

  14. The elastic net is logistic regression with a penalty that shrinks coefficients and sets many to zero, so it can use more features than samples; glmnet is the R package that fits it.↩︎

  15. The AI agent that ran the pilot, wrote the files this document is built from, and kept a log of its decisions.↩︎
